Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

He is receiving ifosfamide, cisplatin and etoposide (ICE). Desmopressin, hydrocortisone and levothyroxine are continued. Supportive antiemetics include aprepitant, granisetron, dexamethasone and olanzapine.

Before salvage chemotherapy: serum sodium 139.3 mEq/L, measured serum osmolality 278 mOsm/kg and creatinine 0.52 mg/dL. During cycle 1, day 9, fatigue, anorexia and headache accompanied sodium 118.4 mEq/L and measured osmolality 236 mOsm/kg.

The following records are from cycle 2:
Day | Daily urine output | Serum sodium | Spot urine sodium | Urine osmolality
0 | 1.40 L/day | Not supplied | Not supplied | Not supplied
3 | 4.25 L/day | 124.4 mEq/L | 241.8 mEq/L | 617 mOsm/kg
4 | 9.75 L/day | 123.3 mEq/L | 196.2 mEq/L | 541 mOsm/kg

Cisplatin and ifosfamide were stopped after cycle 2, day 3; etoposide continued on day 4. Assess the case using information through day 4 only. Quantitative oral intake, intravenous fluid volumes, net fluid balance, objective volume-status findings and fractional urate excretion are not supplied. Exact sampling and result-availability times are not supplied.", "original_task": "Audience: the treating clinical team. Write 150–220 words in English. Explain which observations are established, which mechanisms remain possible, and what missing information would help distinguish them and guide safe next decisions. Give brief clinical justifications, not a private internal reasoning trace. Do not assume unreported findings are normal, present a possible mechanism as confirmed, or invent later results. Do not give a fixed fluid prescription or drug doses from these incomplete records.", "audience": "Clinical team", "task_mode": "written", "actual_dialogue_and_public_notes": [], "closing_public_assessment_note": {}, "final_answer_unchanged": "Main problem: Severe hyponatremia with progressive polyuria and inappropriately concentrated, sodium-rich urine during salvage chemotherapy in a patient with central diabetes insipidus.

Chronology: Daily urine output rose from 1.40 L/day (day 0) to 9.75 L/day (day 4), an absolute increase of 8.35 L/day (596.4%). Serum sodium fell from 124.4 to 123.3 mEq/L over days 3–4.

Established: Hyponatremia with low serum osmolality, high urine osmolality (541–617 mOsm/kg), and markedly elevated spot urine sodium (196–242 mEq/L) coexist with progressive polyuria. Cisplatin and ifosfamide were stopped after day 3.

Possible mechanisms: Cerebral salt wasting or cisplatin-induced renal salt wasting could explain polyuria with high urine sodium and concentrated urine. SIADH alone is less consistent with polyuria. Desmopressin breakthrough with concurrent salt wasting remains possible. These are hypotheses, not confirmed diagnoses.
